# SDF-based Neural Fields
Also called: SDF NeRF, Signed Distance Function Neural Fields

## Overview
SDF-based Neural Fields replace the standard volume density $\sigma$ with a Signed Distance Function ([SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md)) $s(\mathbf{x})$ to provide a more explicit and smooth formulation of surfaces, addressing the geometric inaccuracy and surface holes typical of density-based NeRFs [S1, unofficial]. Unlike [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) which models opacity as a continuous accumulation, this family defines geometry via the zero-level set $\{ \mathbf{x} \mid s(\mathbf{x}) = 0 \}$, enabling sharper boundaries and better topological consistency [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves replacing the density prediction $\sigma$ with an SDF prediction $s(\mathbf{x})$. A signed distance function is a 3D representation based on a continuous scalar field $s: \mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, where for each 3D point $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$, the function value $s(\mathbf{x})$ gives the distance to the closest surface, with the sign conventionally negative inside the object and positive outside [S1, unofficial]. The surface itself is thus defined as the zero-level set $\{ \mathbf{x} \mid s(\mathbf{x}) = 0 \}$ [S1, unofficial].

In SDF-based neural fields, instead of predicting a density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ directly, the network predicts an SDF value $s(\mathbf{x})$, which is then converted into a density to enable volumetric rendering [S1, unofficial]. The conversion typically involves a softplus or sigmoid function to map the unbounded SDF values to positive density values suitable for the [volume rendering integral](#8682-volume-rendering-integral.md). Let $\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = \text{softplus}(s(\mathbf{x}))$ or $\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = \text{sigmoid}(s(\mathbf{x})) \cdot \beta$ where $\beta$ is a temperature parameter [G]. This allows the use of standard [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) pipelines while enforcing geometric priors.

The rendering equation remains:
$$
\hat{C}(r) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{c}_i
$$
where $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$ and $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ [S1, unofficial]. The key difference lies in the source of $\sigma_i$, derived from $s(\mathbf{x}_i)$ rather than a direct MLP output.

## Background
The concept of combining [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) with Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) emerged as a prominent research direction to improve surface quality [S1, unofficial]. Several strategies have been proposed to improve surface quality, ranging from [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) to depth-guided supervision [S1, unofficial]. A prominent research direction [130, 196, 177, 95, 179] has focused on representing geometry by combining NeRF with Signed Distance Functions (SDFs), which provide a more explicit and smooth formulation of surfaces [S1, unofficial]. This approach addresses the limitations of density-based NeRFs, which often suffer from geometric inaccuracies and surface holes [S1, unofficial].
